description.value: The study examined brain activation and heart rate variability as markers of autonomic function during paced breathing, psychosocial stress induction, and stress recovery.

design.value: Each participant underwent a single MRI-scanning session during which they performed a paced-breathing and stress induction task. Brain activation was assessed with fMRI, heart rate variability was assessed continuously using photoplethysmography, and associations with psychometric measures, brain activity, and directional coupling were examined.

description.value: 35 healthy participants were recruited through community advertisements. Three participants were excluded due to excessive head movement during scanning, leading to a sample size of N = 32.

inclusion_criteria.value: no neurological disorder or head injury

exclusion_criteria.value: excessive head movement during scanning (> 4 mm, ± 3° of rotation)

clinical_characteristics.value: No mental illness history; no neurological disorder or head injury.

task_description.value: The task began with 4 min of unpaced breathing, followed by 4 min of normal-paced breathing at 10 breaths/min, 4 min of deep-paced breathing at 5.5 breaths/min, the Montreal Imaging Stress Task, and a 4-min recovery-from-stress block of deep-breathing at 5.5 breaths/min.

presentation_software.value: Presentation V18 (Neurobehavioral Systems, Berkeley, Calif., USA)

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to follow a paced breathing exercise and to solve simple arithmetic tasks and submit their response via a response button box.

stimuli.value: Visual breathing cues, simple arithmetic problems, and feedback indicating whether responses were correct, incorrect, or too slow, together with a manipulated mock performance bar.

instrument.value: Prisma Fit 3-T whole-body MR scanner (Siemens Medical Solutions, Erlangen, Germany) equipped with a standard 32-channel head coil

description.value: 40 oblique interleaved slices were acquired parallel to the AC-PC axis using a T2*-sensitive single-shot EPI sequence. A total of 500 images were collected during one single run. High-resolution T1 MPRAGE anatomical images were also acquired for anatomical reference.

Heart rate was continuously monitored during scanning using a PPG sensor attached to the proximal phalanx of the left index finger. Local maxima of the PPG signal were automatically detected, and timestamps of PPG peaks were recorded by the MR scanner.

description.value: Respiration was continuously measured using inductive plethysmography via a respiratory cushion integrated into a belt fitted around the participant's ribcage. The cushion was connected by a pressure hose to the ECG and respiratory sensor unit (PERU), which recorded respiration curves in real time.

model_settings.value: Block design with task events modeled using boxcar functions and a 480 s high-pass filter. Individual contrast images were constructed for Relaxation, Stress Reactivity, Stress Recovery Specific Relaxation, Post Stress Relaxation, and additional baseline comparisons.

estimator.value: One-sample T-tests at the group level; paired T-tests comparing first-level results with and without HRV regressors

model_settings.value: Brain activation time series from seven a priori defined ROIs were included as smooth terms to predict RMSSD and IBI. Experimental condition, subjects, and time points were included as parametric terms. Thin plate regression splines were used, smoothing parameters were estimated using restricted maximum likelihood, and subject and condition were included as fixed effects in the final models.

For each HRV–ROI pair, vector autoregressive models were fitted. The optimal lag order for each bivariate model was determined using the Akaike Information Criterion. Statistical significance was evaluated using 1,000 permutations generated by independently shuffling HRV and ROI time series across time points, with Bonferroni correction.

estimator.value: vector autoregressive models with permutation-based null distributions

model_settings.value: Two-tailed correlations between differences in IBI and RMSSD across experimental conditions and individual scores on PSS, TICS-SCSS, and STAI scales; P < 0.05.
